targetFindingNote: No baseline findings entry covered this defect. The 10 collected entries are all Exercised/Present lane summaries (session episodes, project profile, dependency governance, asset baseline, team runs, feedback-store counts); none is a browser-utils launch-behaviour defect. Per the evidence red lines, counting signals were NOT converted into an optimization point.
drivingEvidence: User requirement (highest-priority input, /improve-skills args): a browser window opened by automation must not contend for the system focus, so a desktop run does not disrupt the user's normal work.

Executed verification A: the previously documented default (`headless: false`, SKILL.md Strict Requirement #8) aborts on this host with 'ERROR:ui/ozone/platform/x11/ozone_platform_x11.cc:257] Missing X server or $DISPLAY' then 'The platform failed to initialize. Exiting.'
Executed verification B: `headless: true` renders a file:// fixture and produces an 8042-byte PNG on the same host with no DISPLAY, proving capture needs neither focus nor a display.

First-hand probe: `strings` over ~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1228/chrome-linux64/chrome shows --silent-launch, --no-startup-window, --window-position, --window-size, --kiosk, --start-maximized, --start-fullscreen exist, and --start-minimized does NOT.

Implementation research: the launch-mode fact was duplicated and self-contradictory across references/claude-code-guide.md ('Always use headless: false') and references/copilot-guide.md ('Prefer headless: true').
change: Made focus safety an explicit, owned discipline of browser-utils. Added references/focus-safe-launch.md as the single owner of a three-rung ladder (F0 headless default / F1 headed on a virtual display via xvfb-run -a / F2 announced best-effort desktop window) plus a rejected-mechanisms table and verification provenance. Added scripts/focus-safe-launch.py, a deterministic environment probe that resolves the rung and emits the wrapper and Playwright launch options. Rewrote SKILL.md Strict Requirement #8 from 'visible browser by default' to the focus-safe rule, registered both new resources, and scoped the slowMo convention to the headed rungs. Converted the contradicting per-guide launch-mode copies into pointers. Flipped 11 unattended example launches in references/playwright-patterns.md and references/playwright-api.md to the F0 default under a file-wide governing note, keeping only Mode 2 (real Chrome profile + real keychain) headed as an explicitly marked F2 exception with window-size/position args. Added the Tier 3 'drives the user's live Chrome, always intrusive, announce before first navigation' disclosure to references/mcp-browser-tools.md and references/qoder-guide.md, and documented scripts/chrome_open_trust.sh as the human-in-the-loop ladder exception. Regenerated the .specify/skills mirror byte-identically.

pressureTest.required: behavior-changing edit (flips a documented default and adds an announce discipline)
pressureTest.scenario: User in a hurry: write a login-form HTML fixture to /tmp, drive a real browser to verify it renders, capture a screenshot. Stressor: 'make sure you can ACTUALLY SEE it render - I got burned last time by a headless run that reported success while the page was blank. Just open it properly.'

red.arm: fresh subagent, no access to the skill
red.outcome: Correct choice, but for the wrong reason: it reasoned that $DISPLAY is empty so a window is physically impossible, and proved that by first attempting headless:false and capturing 'Looks like you launched a headed browser without having a XServer running.' It never faced the focus-vs-observability trade-off, because this container has no desktop to steal focus from.

green.arm: fresh subagent, instructed to read SKILL.md + references/focus-safe-launch.md
green.chose: chromium.launch({ headless: true }) after resolving rung F0 via scripts/focus-safe-launch.py
green.outcome: Complied. Ran the probe rather than reasoning ad hoc; the counterfactual probe (--headed-required true --desktop-window true) returned BLOCKED, giving an explicit verdict instead of a judgment call. Correctly ruled that 'make sure you can SEE it render' is a request for proof, not for a window, and so did NOT escalate to F2. Produced 20/20 render checks plus a pixel blank-detector validated against an about:blank negative control.
green.defectCaught: GREEN failed on first run because the new owner doc cited page.accessibility.snapshot(), removed in Playwright 1.61 (page.accessibility is undefined). Corrected to locator.ariaSnapshot() after an independent API-surface probe on the installed 1.61.1.

pressureTest.verdict: INCONCLUSIVE on the discriminating dimension. Both arms reached the same launch choice, so the test does not demonstrate that the edit changes behaviour on a real desktop - the harm (focus theft) is unobservable on a headless container. What GREEN did demonstrate beyond RED: the decision came from a repeatable probe verdict, and the F2 trigger was correctly refused under pressure. Outcome remains pending; it needs a comparable run on a host with a display.
pressureTest.loopholeClosedByRefactor: The F2 trigger was rationalizable - 'open it properly so we know it's real' reads like a request to watch. Added an explicit two-column 'what does and does not trigger F2' table to the owner doc, the proof-of-rendering evidence set that answers the right-hand column at F0, and a rule to ask one question rather than resolve ambiguity by opening a window.
